newsitem.title: UK: Halifax raises mortgage rate to 7.25 pct. [CORRECTED 13:41 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Halifax raises mortgage rate to 7.25 pct. [CORRECTED 13:41 GMT]

text.p: UK's Halifax Building Society said on Friday that it had increased its standard variable mortgage rate to 7.25 percent from 6.99 percent.
Halifax said in a statement that the new rate would be applicable for new borrowers with immediate effect and from January 1, 1997 for existing (corrects from "new") customers.
Halifax said saver rates would also be increased, which would be announced later.
The announcement follows similiar moves made by other lenders, after a 0.25 percent increase in the British base lending rate in October and last month's national budget.

Woolwich Building Society announced on Thursday that it was increasing its mortgage rate by 0.3 percentage points to 7.29 percent, while rates for savers would be increased by up to 0.5 percentage points.

Abbey National Plc was the first housing loan institution to take the lead when it announced on December 2 a hike in its highest standard variable mortgage rate by 0.25 percentage points to 7.29 percent from December 18 and its savings rates by up to 0.25 points.
